topics.name: Choice of Law
topics.description: Clauses selecting which jurisdiction's substantive law governs disputes or the interpretation of the terms.

scores.label: bad
scores.explanation: The ToS provides that a law other than the law of the user's habitual residence will apply to disputes arising in connection with the contract.

scores.label: neutral
scores.explanation: The ToS applies another law only to businesses, or expressly preserves the mandatory consumer protections of the user's habitual residence.

scores.label: good
scores.explanation: No foreign choice-of-law clause is imposed, or the governing law is the law of the user's habitual residence.

topics.name: Choice of Forum
topics.description: Clauses selecting the court, venue, or jurisdiction where disputes must be brought.

scores.label: bad
scores.explanation: The ToS requires disputes to be resolved in courts outside the user's place of permanent residence or domicile.

scores.label: neutral
scores.explanation: A foreign forum is imposed only on businesses, or the clause is ambiguous but preserves mandatory consumer forum protections.

scores.label: good
scores.explanation: No foreign forum is imposed, or the user may bring claims in the courts of their domicile.

topics.name: Mandatory Arbitration
topics.description: Clauses requiring disputes to be filed in arbitration rather than ordinary courts.

scores.label: bad
scores.explanation: The user must bring claims before an arbitration tribunal specified in the ToS instead of filing a traditional court lawsuit.

scores.label: neutral
scores.explanation: Arbitration is mandatory only for businesses or only in limited jurisdictions while preserving consumers' access to court.

scores.label: good
scores.explanation: The ToS does not impose mandatory arbitration, or arbitration is offered only as a voluntary option.

topics.name: Class Action Waiver
topics.description: Clauses preventing users from bringing or joining collective, representative, or class proceedings.

scores.label: bad
scores.explanation: The ToS forbids the user from participating in a group or class of people collectively filing a civil claim.

scores.label: neutral
scores.explanation: The waiver is limited to businesses, specific jurisdictions, or only applies to the extent permitted by law.

scores.label: good
scores.explanation: The ToS contains no class action waiver and does not restrict collective redress.

topics.name: Limitation of Liability
topics.description: Clauses limiting or excluding the company's liability for damages connected with use of the service.

scores.label: bad
scores.explanation: The company unlawfully limits liability for personal injury, non-performance against consumers, intentionally caused damage, or other mandatory liability.

scores.label: neutral
scores.explanation: The limitation appears lawful, for example excluding losses not caused by the company's breach or limiting liability only where permitted by law.

scores.label: good
scores.explanation: The ToS does not limit the company's liability or expressly preserves mandatory liability.

topics.name: Liability Cap
topics.description: Clauses setting a maximum amount recoverable from the company for damages.

scores.label: bad
scores.explanation: All users entitled to damages connected with using the service may claim damages only up to a fixed amount.

scores.label: neutral
scores.explanation: Only businesses, or only non-consumer claims, are subject to a fixed damages cap.

scores.label: good
scores.explanation: There is no maximum damages amount, or mandatory consumer remedies are expressly uncapped.

topics.name: Warranty Disclaimer
topics.description: Clauses providing the service on an as-is basis or disclaiming warranties, guarantees, service quality, availability, or fitness for purpose.

scores.label: bad
scores.explanation: The service is provided as-is and all warranties or guarantees are disclaimed, including mandatory consumer conformity rights.

scores.label: neutral
scores.explanation: Warranties are limited only to the extent permitted by law, or the clause is qualified while preserving mandatory statutory guarantees.

scores.label: good
scores.explanation: The ToS lacks an as-is disclaimer or expressly guarantees defined service features, quality, availability, or statutory conformity rights.

topics.name: Indemnification
topics.description: Clauses requiring the user to compensate, defend, or hold the company harmless from claims, losses, damages, or expenses.

scores.label: bad
scores.explanation: The user must broadly indemnify the company for claims or losses beyond the user's fault, unlawful conduct, or clear breach of the terms.

scores.label: neutral
scores.explanation: An indemnification clause is present but limited to third-party claims or direct claims caused by the user's unlawful conduct or clear breach.

scores.label: good
scores.explanation: The ToS imposes no indemnification obligation on the user.

topics.name: Limitation Period
topics.description: Clauses shortening or setting a time limit for bringing claims against the company.

scores.label: bad
scores.explanation: The ToS sets a contractual time limit for bringing a claim to court and bars claims after that period.

scores.label: neutral
scores.explanation: The ToS does not contain a contractual limitation period or only restates generally applicable statutory limitation rules.

scores.label: good
scores.explanation: The ToS expressly preserves the user's full statutory limitation period or gives the user a longer period than applicable law requires.

topics.name: Contract Changes
topics.description: Clauses allowing the company to amend the Terms of Service or contractual obligations.

scores.label: bad
scores.explanation: The company reserves the right to change the contract at any time without a valid reason stated in the contract.

scores.label: neutral
scores.explanation: The company may change the contract for stated reasons, but the reasons are vague, incomplete, or leave broad discretion.

scores.label: good
scores.explanation: Contract changes require valid reasons specified in the contract, genuine user agreement, or the company reserves no unilateral change right.

topics.name: Service Changes
topics.description: Clauses allowing the company to modify the service, features, design, availability, or functionality.

scores.label: bad
scores.explanation: The company may change the service without valid reasons or without any stated requirements, including adding, removing, or modifying features at will.

scores.label: neutral
scores.explanation: The company may change the service for vague or broadly stated reasons that are hard for consumers to evaluate.

scores.label: good
scores.explanation: Service changes are limited to valid reasons specified in the contract, require appropriate notice or consent, or no unilateral change right is reserved.

topics.name: Price Changes
topics.description: Clauses allowing unilateral changes to prices, fees, subscription charges, or other payment terms.

scores.label: bad
scores.explanation: The company may change prices for existing or future services without valid reasons, advance notice, or a meaningful right to cancel before the change applies.

scores.label: neutral
scores.explanation: The company reserves the right to change future prices for services not yet supplied or enabled, but the user's cancellation or notice rights are limited.

scores.label: good
scores.explanation: The company does not reserve unilateral future price changes, or price changes require clear advance notice and a meaningful right to reject or terminate.

topics.name: Notice of Changes
topics.description: Clauses describing whether users receive clear and advance notice before changes to terms or policies take effect.

scores.label: bad
scores.explanation: Terms may change without prior notice, take effect immediately, or be accepted automatically through continued use.

scores.label: neutral
scores.explanation: Users are notified of changes, but without enough lead time or without a meaningful opportunity to review and decide before they take effect.

scores.label: good
scores.explanation: Users receive clear advance notice, a reasonable review period, and the ability to terminate before changed terms apply.

topics.name: User Participation in Changes
topics.description: Clauses indicating whether users can participate, provide meaningful feedback, or consent before substantial changes are imposed.

scores.label: bad
scores.explanation: Changes are imposed unilaterally on a take-it-or-leave-it basis, with continued use deemed acceptance and no user consultation.

scores.label: neutral
scores.explanation: Users may provide feedback or are consulted on some changes, but the company retains final unilateral discretion.

scores.label: good
scores.explanation: Substantial changes require genuine user agreement or meaningful consultation, giving users a real role in the change process.

topics.name: Account Termination
topics.description: Clauses allowing the company to delete an account or terminate the contract unilaterally.

scores.label: bad
scores.explanation: The company may delete the user's account or terminate the contract without serious grounds or a reasonable notice period.

scores.label: neutral
scores.explanation: Termination requires either serious grounds without notice or notice without serious grounds, but not both.

scores.label: good
scores.explanation: Termination is limited to serious grounds with reasonable notice, or the company reserves no unilateral termination right.

topics.name: Account Suspension
topics.description: Clauses allowing the company to suspend, restrict, or disable the user's account or access to the service.

scores.label: bad
scores.explanation: The company may suspend the user's account without serious grounds, prior notice, or an appeal or redress mechanism.

scores.label: neutral
scores.explanation: Suspension is tied to stated grounds but lacks notice or appeal, or includes notice but relies on broad or vague grounds.

scores.label: good
scores.explanation: Suspension is limited to serious specified grounds with notice, reasons, and appeal rights, or no suspension right is reserved.

topics.name: Content Removal
topics.description: Clauses allowing the company to remove, delete, censor, restrict, or moderate user content.

scores.label: bad
scores.explanation: The company may delete or censor all user content without restrictions, serious grounds, notice, or appeal.

scores.label: neutral
scores.explanation: The company may remove content only for illegality or Terms violations, but the grounds or procedure remain broad or incomplete.

scores.label: good
scores.explanation: The company does not reserve a content-removal right, or removal is limited to serious specified grounds with reasons, notice, and redress.

topics.name: Contract Formed Through Use
topics.description: Clauses stating that visiting, downloading, accessing, browsing, or using the service constitutes acceptance of the Terms.

scores.label: bad
scores.explanation: The user is deemed bound merely by visiting, browsing, downloading, or continuing to use the service, without clear presentation of the terms or an affirmative act of acceptance.

scores.label: neutral
scores.explanation: Use of the service may constitute acceptance, but the terms are reasonably available and the user receives some notice before or during sign-up.

scores.label: good
scores.explanation: The user is bound only after clear notice of the terms and an affirmative, informed acceptance action.

topics.name: Privacy Policy Incorporation
topics.description: Clauses incorporating the privacy policy into the terms, or stating that use of the service also means consent to privacy practices.

scores.label: bad
scores.explanation: The ToS treats privacy-policy consent as automatic through use of the service, without separate, informed, specific, and freely given consent where required.

scores.label: neutral
scores.explanation: The privacy policy is incorporated by reference and linked, but the relationship between contractual acceptance and privacy consent is not fully clear.

scores.label: good
scores.explanation: The ToS clearly distinguishes contractual acceptance from privacy choices and preserves separate consent or lawful-basis requirements for data processing.

topics.name: Copyright License
topics.description: Clauses granting the company a license to use, host, reproduce, modify, distribute, sublicense, or exploit user content.

scores.label: bad
scores.explanation: The user grants a broad, perpetual, irrevocable, sublicensable, or commercially exploitable license beyond what is necessary to provide the service.

scores.label: neutral
scores.explanation: The license is broader than strictly necessary, but its purposes are listed and explained, or necessity is uncertain.

scores.label: good
scores.explanation: Any license is limited to what is necessary to operate and provide the service, or no user-content license is required.

topics.name: Ownership
topics.description: Clauses describing ownership of content, data, or other material generated or uploaded by the user.

scores.label: bad
scores.explanation: The ToS claims ownership of, or assigns title in, user-generated content or personal data to the company.

scores.label: neutral
scores.explanation: The user nominally retains ownership, but the clause is ambiguous or grants such broad company rights that practical control is reduced.

scores.label: good
scores.explanation: The ToS expressly confirms that users retain full ownership of and title to their generated content and personal data.

topics.name: Content Retrieval
topics.description: Clauses describing whether users may retrieve, export, download, or recover their digital content after termination or account closure.

scores.label: bad
scores.explanation: The ToS lacks a clause ensuring the user's right to retrieve their digital content after termination.

scores.label: neutral
scores.explanation: The user may retrieve only some digital content, or retrieval is limited, unclear, or burdensome.

scores.label: good
scores.explanation: The user can retrieve all of their digital content after termination in a practical and accessible manner.

topics.name: Feedback Reuse
topics.description: Clauses allowing the company to use, incorporate, exploit, or commercialize user feedback, ideas, or suggestions without compensation.

scores.label: bad
scores.explanation: The company obtains broad ownership or an irrevocable license over user feedback or suggestions without compensation and without meaningful limits.

scores.label: neutral
scores.explanation: The company may incorporate user feedback or suggestions without compensation, but the permission is limited to improving or operating the service.

scores.label: good
scores.explanation: The company does not claim a right to use user feedback without compensation, or use requires separate permission.

topics.name: Transfer of Contract
topics.description: Clauses allowing contractual rights or obligations to be assigned, transferred, or delegated to another entity.

scores.label: bad
scores.explanation: The ToS allows the company to transfer contractual rights or obligations to another entity without the user's consent.

scores.label: neutral
scores.explanation: The company may transfer rights with user consent or notice, but the user lacks equivalent transfer rights.

scores.label: good
scores.explanation: Transfers require user consent and reciprocal fairness, or the ToS contains no company transfer right.

topics.name: Business Transfer
topics.description: Clauses describing transfers of user data, accounts, or rights in connection with mergers, acquisitions, reorganizations, or asset sales.

scores.label: bad
scores.explanation: User data or accounts may be transferred in a merger, acquisition, or asset sale without notice, consent, or an ability to object.

scores.label: neutral
scores.explanation: Business-transfer data sharing is disclosed and subject to notice or existing commitments, but the user has limited control.

scores.label: good
scores.explanation: Any business-transfer data sharing requires advance notice and a meaningful ability to object, withdraw, delete, or export data.

topics.name: Personal Data
topics.description: Clauses describing collection, use, retention, control, and rights over personal data.

scores.label: bad
scores.explanation: The user has no meaningful control over how personal data is used or retained, and data may be processed for incompatible purposes.

scores.label: neutral
scores.explanation: Some data subject rights or controls are provided, but they are limited, burdensome, or paired with vague purposes or retention rules.

scores.label: good
scores.explanation: The user has meaningful control consistent with rights of access, rectification, erasure, restriction, objection, portability, purpose limitation, and storage limitation.

topics.name: Trackers
topics.description: Clauses describing cookies, pixels, device identifiers, fingerprinting, geolocation, session storage, advertising IDs, and other tracking technologies.

scores.label: bad
scores.explanation: The service uses extensive tracking without adequate disclosure, lawful basis, or an easy ability to refuse non-essential tracking.

scores.label: neutral
scores.explanation: Trackers are disclosed and some consent or opt-out is offered, but non-essential tracking is enabled by default or hard to refuse.

scores.label: good
scores.explanation: Only strictly necessary trackers are used, or non-essential tracking requires informed opt-in consent that is as easy to refuse as to give.

topics.name: Anonymity
topics.description: Clauses describing whether users may use the service anonymously or pseudonymously and what identifying information is required.

scores.label: bad
scores.explanation: The service requires verified real-identity registration, prohibits pseudonymous use, and collects extensive identifying information.

scores.label: neutral
scores.explanation: Pseudonymous use is allowed, but some real-identity verification is required or collection exceeds what is necessary.

scores.label: good
scores.explanation: The service can be used anonymously or pseudonymously with only minimal identifying data.

topics.name: Types of Information Collected
topics.description: Clauses describing categories of information collected from users voluntarily, automatically, or from third parties.

scores.label: bad
scores.explanation: The categories of information collected are undisclosed, open-ended, or excessive relative to what the service requires.

scores.label: neutral
scores.explanation: Categories of information are disclosed but only broadly or vaguely, or collection exceeds what is necessary.

scores.label: good
scores.explanation: Categories of information collected are clear, specific, and limited to what is necessary to provide the service.

topics.name: Third Parties
topics.description: Clauses describing sharing, sale, disclosure, processing, or transfer of user data by third parties such as processors, partners, social networks, advertisers, or analytics providers.

scores.label: bad
scores.explanation: Personal data is shared with or sold to third parties without disclosure, lawful basis, or user control.

scores.label: neutral
scores.explanation: Third-party sharing is disclosed and limited to stated purposes, but user control is limited.

scores.label: good
scores.explanation: Third-party sharing is minimal, transparent, purpose-bound, and subject to user control or consent, with no sale of personal data.

topics.name: Advertising
topics.description: Clauses describing advertising practices, ad targeting, profiling, ad partners, and user controls over advertising.

scores.label: bad
scores.explanation: Personal data is used for advertising, profiling, or targeting without disclosure, lawful basis, opt-out, or limits on third-party involvement.

scores.label: neutral
scores.explanation: Targeted advertising is disclosed and some opt-out exists, but it is enabled by default or relies on extensive personal-data sharing.

scores.label: good
scores.explanation: Advertising is non-targeted, or uses personal data only with informed opt-in consent, easy opt-out, and minimal third-party involvement.

topics.name: Government Requests
topics.description: Clauses describing disclosure of user data to governments, courts, regulators, law enforcement, or other public authorities.

scores.label: bad
scores.explanation: The service may disclose user data to governments or law enforcement without valid legal process, user notice, or transparency reporting.

scores.label: neutral
scores.explanation: Disclosure is limited to valid legal requests, but the service provides no user notice or transparency reporting.

scores.label: good
scores.explanation: Disclosure is limited to valid legal process with notice where lawful, transparency reporting, and a commitment to challenge overbroad requests.

topics.name: Logs
topics.description: Clauses describing collection and retention of logs, connection data, access records, IP addresses, or similar technical records.

scores.label: bad
scores.explanation: Log or connection-data retention is undisclosed or indefinite.

scores.label: neutral
scores.explanation: A retention period is disclosed but is lengthy, vague, or not clearly tied to a specified purpose.

scores.label: good
scores.explanation: Logs are retained only for a clearly stated, limited, purpose-bound period, or are not retained and are promptly deleted or anonymized.

topics.name: Right to Leave the Service
topics.description: Clauses describing whether the user can terminate, leave, delete data, export content, avoid lock-in, or close an account.

scores.label: bad
scores.explanation: The user cannot freely terminate, delete data, or retrieve content, creating lock-in.

scores.label: neutral
scores.explanation: The user may leave and delete or retrieve some data or content, but the process is partial, burdensome, or unclear.

scores.label: good
scores.explanation: The user may freely terminate and retrieve or delete their data and content, with practical portability support.

topics.name: Complaint Handling System
topics.description: Clauses describing an internal complaint-handling, appeal, or redress system for company decisions affecting users.

scores.label: bad
scores.explanation: There is no internal complaint-handling system for company decisions affecting the user's contractual rights before going to court or another institution.

scores.label: neutral
scores.explanation: A complaint-handling system exists but does not meet all requirements for accessibility, precision, substantiation, timeliness, or usability.

scores.label: good
scores.explanation: A free, electronic, easy-to-access, user-friendly complaint-handling system is available for a sufficient period and enables precise, substantiated complaints.

topics.name: Recommender System Transparency
topics.description: Clauses explaining the main parameters of automated or partially automated recommender systems and user options to influence them.

scores.label: bad
scores.explanation: The ToS does not set out the main parameters used by recommender systems to suggest or prioritize information.

scores.label: neutral
scores.explanation: The ToS sets out recommender parameters, but not in a clear, accessible, and easily comprehensible manner.

scores.label: good
scores.explanation: The ToS clearly explains recommender parameters and any user options to modify or influence them, including at least one option not based on profiling where applicable.

topics.name: Discretionary Interpretation
topics.description: Clauses reserving exclusive or unilateral power for the company to interpret the Terms.

scores.label: bad
scores.explanation: The company reserves the exclusive right to interpret any term of the contract by itself.

scores.label: neutral
scores.explanation: The ToS lacks a discretionary interpretation clause, or interpretation authority is ambiguous but not expressly exclusive to the company.

scores.label: good
scores.explanation: Interpretation is not controlled unilaterally by the company and consumer-protective or mutual interpretation principles are preserved.

topics.name: Interpretation Clause
topics.description: Clauses describing how ambiguous or disputed terms should be interpreted.

scores.label: bad
scores.explanation: The ToS states that the contract must be interpreted in favor of the company's intent.

scores.label: neutral
scores.explanation: The ToS states that interpretation should reflect both parties' intent, or provides a balanced general interpretation rule.

scores.label: good
scores.explanation: The ToS states that ambiguity or interpretation should favor the consumer or user.

topics.name: Severability
topics.description: Clauses stating what happens if one or more provisions are unconstitutional, void, invalid, or unenforceable.

scores.label: bad
scores.explanation: The severability clause lets the company unilaterally replace, rewrite, or preserve the economic effect of invalid or unfair terms.

scores.label: neutral
scores.explanation: The ToS keeps the remaining contract in force if a court declares one or more provisions void, invalid, unconstitutional, or unenforceable.

scores.label: good
scores.explanation: The ToS lacks a severability clause or expressly provides that invalid consumer-unfair terms will not be replaced to the user's detriment.

topics.name: Content Rules
topics.description: Clauses defining what users are allowed or prohibited to post, publish, upload, share, or discuss.

scores.label: bad
scores.explanation: Content restrictions are broad, vague, or discretionary enough to unduly restrict lawful expression or permit arbitrary enforcement.

scores.label: neutral
scores.explanation: Content rules are defined but remain broad, leaving significant interpretive discretion to the company.

scores.label: good
scores.explanation: Content rules are clear, specific, limited to unlawful or genuinely harmful content, and predictably enforced.

topics.name: Service Governance
topics.description: Clauses describing how the service, community, moderation, rules, decisions, and accountability structures are governed.

scores.label: bad
scores.explanation: The company retains wholly unilateral and discretionary governance with no user participation, published decision-making criteria, or accountability mechanisms.

scores.label: neutral
scores.explanation: Some governance structures exist, such as guidelines or moderation rules, but users have no meaningful voice and enforcement remains discretionary.

scores.label: good
scores.explanation: The service provides transparent governance with meaningful participation, published criteria, and accessible appeal or redress procedures.

topics.name: Transparency
topics.description: Clauses and policy language affecting whether users receive clear, plain, accessible, and comprehensible information about terms and practices.

scores.label: bad
scores.explanation: Terms or policies are inaccessible, unclear, hidden, or not drafted in plain and intelligible language.

scores.label: neutral
scores.explanation: Information is provided but incomplete, dense, hard to navigate, or insufficient for informed user understanding.

scores.label: good
scores.explanation: Terms and practices are presented in clear, plain, accessible, and easily comprehensible language.

topics.name: Security
topics.description: Clauses describing technical, organizational, account, and breach-related security measures.

scores.label: bad
scores.explanation: The ToS describes no security measures or disclaims responsibility for protecting the user's account and data against unauthorized access.

scores.label: neutral
scores.explanation: Basic security measures are mentioned, but commitments are vague or place most responsibility on the user.

scores.label: good
scores.explanation: The service commits to appropriate technical and organizational security measures, including breach handling and notification where required.

topics.name: Payments
topics.description: Clauses describing payment obligations, recurring charges, automatic renewal, payment credentials, cancellation, and refunds.

scores.label: bad
scores.explanation: The ToS imposes recurring charges, auto-renewal, or payment credential storage without clear consent, accessible cancellation, or refund rights.

scores.label: neutral
scores.explanation: Recurring payments or auto-renewal are disclosed, but cancellation or refund rights are limited or burdensome.

scores.label: good
scores.explanation: Payment terms are transparent, recurring charges require explicit consent, cancellation and refund rights are accessible, or no payment obligation is imposed.

topics.name: Unclassified
topics.description: Fallback topic for clauses that must be retained during exhaustive annotation but do not fit any curated Lawgic topic. Prefer omitting unmatched clauses from notable_clauses when the pipeline does not require exhaustive classification.

scores.label: bad
scores.explanation: The clause appears materially harmful to the user, but it does not fit any curated Lawgic topic.

scores.label: neutral
scores.explanation: The clause is relevant to the terms but does not clearly create either a user-harmful or user-beneficial rule within the curated taxonomy.

scores.label: good
scores.explanation: The clause appears materially beneficial to the user, but it does not fit any curated Lawgic topic.
